title: Multi-Layer Networks
motto: One neuron draws a line. Stack them, and you can draw anything.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: One neuron draws a line. Stack them, and you can draw anything.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: A single neuron is a line drawer. That's it. One straight line through your data. Every real problem in AI -- image recognition, language understanding, playing Go -- requires curves. Stacking neurons into layers is how you get curves.

In 1969, Minsky and Papert proved this limitation was fatal: a single-layer network cannot learn XOR. Not "struggles to learn" -- mathematically cannot. The XOR truth table places [0,1] and [1,0] on one side, [0,0] and [1,1] on the other. No single line separates them.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Hidden layers compose nonlinear transforms. ReLU(x)=max(0,x) is the default activation — cheap and avoids vanishing gradients.
